label: REAL Kapucu 2022 untreated wells: early network state and later settling, human iPSC vs rat (registered replication, D36)

age_check.verdict: registered age flag not raised: the human partial rho is not above -0.1

nonzero_nb0_check_post_hoc.note: post hoc, not registered, added after the first real-data run: is a missing relation only the recordings with no network burst in window 0 (ties at zero)?

primary_pool_post_hoc.label: post hoc, not registered: the exploratory observation that motivated D36, recomputed on D35's usable wells of the two 48-well baselines (one recording a well)

implementation_notes: The replication recordings are read from D32's results file of the same run (hpsc_split_half_REAL.json, pool replication, usable true) as (plate, DIV, well); on a full run without those rows D32's replication table is rebuilt; a --quick run has none and N1-N3 are then uninterpretable with a status.

Windows follow D32 and D35: the plate file's last spike time is the duration, cut into 6 equal windows; window 0 is t < duration / 6 and goes to extract_features with that length; a spike on the edge starts window 1.
nb0, sync0 and mfr0 are extract_features' network_burst_rate_per_min, synchrony_index and mfr_hz on window 0 at FeatureParams defaults; window 0's own active rule selects electrodes.
late_b uses D35's electrode set (active over the whole recording), D35's per-window rate and its one-spike floor; the slope is fitted on y_1..y_5 against k = 1..5.
A recording is scored for a feature when the feature and late_b are both defined; synchrony_index can be undefined with active electrodes (no STTC pair), which leaves only sync0 unscored.
Spearman rho is the Pearson correlation of average ranks; a constant side gives no rho; a bootstrap resample with no rho is dropped from the interval and counted as nonfinite.

Each species' interval uses a fresh generator (seed 20261028); each resample draws that species' wells (plate:well) with replacement and keeps all of a drawn well's recordings; rho(nb0), rho(sync0), rho(mfr0) and the N3 difference come from the same draws.
The N3 difference is computed on the recordings scored for both nb0 and mfr0.
'Lies below 0' is strict (upper end < 0) and 'lies above 0' strict (lower end > 0); N2 passes unless the rat interval's upper end is below 0.

Uninterpretable is read literally: fewer than 30 scored recordings, or fewer than 8 wells among them, for the tested statistic's species; N1 and N3 also when nb0 is exactly 0 in more than 80% of scored human recordings.

The partial Spearman regresses the average ranks of nb0 and of late_b (over the scored recordings) by OLS on an intercept and DIV as a number, and correlates the residuals; the per-DIV rhos pool both plates of a species at the same DIV, and a DIV with fewer than 3 recordings or a constant side gives no rho and is left out of the median.
The post hoc pool is D35's usable wells (from D32's results file), one 30-min recording a well cut into D35's 5-min windows; its intervals use the same well bootstrap.

Added after the first real-data run and labelled post hoc: rho(nb0, late_b) over the recordings with nb0 > 0, the count of negative per-DIV rhos, and the rank correlations of nb0 and of late_b with DIV; the age-check verdict text was reworded to state only whether the registered flag is raised.

Before the code was committed, a timing check computed window-0 features on one developmental plate file (Rat_MEA1 DIV21) and printed one well's values; no late trend or correlation was computed before the commit.
